## Pros

- Toddler seat approved from birth to 50 lb with no add-on (US manual 250127).
- Lightest and smallest folded of the UPPAbaby line, 16.7 lb (maker and BabyGearLab).
- Smooth on pavement and up curbs; CR maneuverability 5/5 (usability note).
- Canopy is large with a mesh window and UPF 50+; stands when folded (BabyGearLab, CR).
- The $99.99 travel bag includes TravelSafe, covering air-travel damage for 4 years (maker).

## Cons

Misuse risks come first.

- **Misuse risk:** the adapter's colour dots show it is on the frame, not that the carrier is latched. Lift the carrier every time (maker; Aria V2 manual).
- **Misuse risk:** newborn use needs the full recline and the rear crotch slot; the seat is not fully flat (157.7°, BabyGearLab), and two reviewers would hesitate with a tiny newborn.
- **Misuse risk:** one owner says the brake held only one wheel (snippet only). Check both wheels.
- No hands-on test of any Aria or Mesa on the Minu V3 found; lock feel, wobble and carrier height unknown.
- Small wheels struggle on gravel, cobbles and grass (CR, MadeForMums, BabyGearLab).
- Handlebar does not adjust; fold is one-handed for some testers but not others.
- Needs a $39.99 adapter for the Aria V2.
- Does not fit the 22 x 14 x 9 in overhead bin on published or measured size, despite the maker's "fits in any overhead bin" claim.
- No bassinet or newborn insert made for it.
- Bumper bar is a $39.99 extra.
- One unverified consumer report (SaferProducts.gov, 2024) says a Minu V2 with Mesa adapters released the car seat going downhill. Older model; lift the carrier to check the latch every time.
